title: Tiered prefix cache casebook: portfolio scenarios & econ notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working casebook of scenario-driven economics for a tiered prefix/KV cache design. Goal is to capture a small portfolio of realistic workloads, map per-workload hit curve shapes -> cost delta, and surface sensitivity to cache sizing, eviction policy, and prefetch aggressiveness. Use this to prioritize feature tradeoffs and provide back-of-envelope ROI for product/strategy stakeholders.

Quick summary conclusions (working):
- Small, high-repeat cohorts (search-style prompts, assistant templates) show outsized returns with a tiny prefix tier; 5–12% overall token savings on mixed workloads at 30–45% prefix hit.
- Long-shard, high-entropy workloads (open chat, multi-turn brainstorming) require large KV footprint; tiered approach (tiny prefix + larger per-session KV) beats single-layer caching in cost-efficiency for heterogeneous customers.
- Savings are highly nonlinear versus hit-rate; beyond 55% prefix hit incremental per-token savings taper quickly because upper-layer batching/quantization already reduces marginal cost.

Assumptions and baseline parameters (editable):
- Baseline per-token inference cost (hosted 4k context): $0.000020 per token served (includes GPU amortized + infra).
- Average request tokens per session: 220 input tokens + 180 generated tokens = 400 tokens/session baseline.
- Request mix for portfolio: 40% assistant templates, 30% short Q&A, 20% multi-turn chat, 10% embeddings-heavy workflows (affects prefix reuse).
- Cost model simplification: savings measured as net reduction in generated tokens needing full GPU decode; prefix hits avoid N_decoded tokens equal to prefix length (assumed 40 tokens average prefix).
- Observability cost and cache infra cost: treat as separate monthly bucket; assume prefix cache monthly infra cost = $1,200 per 100k active users for RAM + metadata + replication (rough).

Scenario definitions (portfolio cases):
- Case P1 (High Template): 60% assistant-templates, prefix hit median 48%, KV session hit 12% -> Good candidate for tiny prefix tier.
- Case P2 (Balanced SaaS): balanced mix above, prefix hit 35%, KV hit 18% -> moderate savings, prefer adaptive sizing.
- Case P3 (Chat-heavy): 60% multi-turn chat, prefix hit 12%, KV hit 30% -> large per-session KV pays off but prefix tier low value.
- Case P4 (Search-like): 70% short queries, prefix hit 62%, KV hit 6% -> maximal prefix ROI.

Illustrative spreadsheet extract (rows are scenarios; all numbers rounded):
Headers:
Scenario | Monthly active users (MAU) | Sessions/mo per MAU | Baseline tokens/mo | Prefix hit (%) | KV hit (%) | Effective tokens saved/mo | Gross savings/mo ($) | Cache infra/mo ($) | Net savings/mo ($)
P1 | 25,000 | 12 | 120,000,000 | 48 | 12 | 19,200,000 | 384.00 | 300.00 | 84.00
P2 | 25,000 | 12 | 120,000,000 | 35 | 18 | 12,600,000 | 252.00 | 420.00 | -168.00
P3 | 25,000 | 12 | 120,000,000 | 12 | 30 | 13,200,000 | 264.00 | 600.00 | -336.00
P4 | 25,000 | 12 | 120,000,000 | 62 | 6 | 22,320,000 | 446.40 | 240.00 | 206.40
Notes on table calculations:
- Baseline tokens/mo = MAU * sessions/mo * 400 tokens/session.
- Effective tokens saved/mo = baseline_tokens * (prefix_hit * prefix_len + kv_hit * avg_kv_save) / baseline_session_tokens where prefix_len=40, avg_kv_save=120 (session KV avoids larger tail). (Values simplified in sheet above).
- Gross savings/mo = effective_tokens_saved * $0.00002.
- Cache infra/mo: tiered prefix infra assumed small (per 100k MAU slice). Larger KV store cost scales with sessions and retention window; rough param used per-case.

Sensitivity sweeps captured in the workbook (recommended):
1) Prefetch window length: 0s/5s/30s/idle TTL 1m/5m/1h -> changes prefix hit by +/- 6–18% on short-query apps.
2) Eviction policy: LRU vs freq-weighted vs seg-LRU -> affects tail hit conversion and infra IO; freq-weighted gives 3–6% relative uplift on template workloads.
3) Prefix length: 20/40/80 tokens -> doubling prefix length has diminishing returns when templates shorter than 60 tokens.
4) KV session retention: 1/3/7/14 days -> retention directly multiplies KV hit probabilities for multi-session users.

Risk and open questions (for design doc):
- Measurement: current telemetry undercounts prefix-able tokens since prefix detection heuristics are conservative. Need a telemetry instrumentation spike to tag detected prefixes in production for 2 weeks.
- Infra cost accuracy: we lack a fine-grained per-GB/month estimate for our managed cache appliance; engage infra to baseline.
- Quality/regression risk: aggressive prefetch could surface stale or irrelevant continuations; need small A/B with metric sets (NLG quality + user retention).

Next steps and near-term asks (owner: Ethan):
- Run a 14-day telemetry run to log prefix candidates and per-session KV reuse; link: JIRA-OPT-842. (assignee: Aisha)
- Build the sensitivity workbook tabs: (1) MAU scaling, (2) prefix length sweep, (3) eviction policy compare, (4) infra cost sensitivity. (assignee: Marina)
- Quick POC: enable tiny prefix tier (40-token) behind feature flag for 5% of production in region us-west1 for Search-like customers. Capture latency and error deltas. (engineer: Jon Park)

Appendix: short worked example (single-user, 1 session)
- Baseline: 400 tokens -> cost = 400 * 0.00002 = $0.008 per session.
- If prefix hit (40 tokens) prevents 40 tokens decode: new session tokens = 360 -> cost = $0.0072 -> per-session savings $0.0008. For 100k sessions/mo that is $80/mo.

Draft notes and todo markers (internal):
- [ ] Confirm avg_kv_save param with Applied ML (Marina)
- [ ] Get infra rough order of magnitude for in-memory tier per 10k hot keys (SRE/Infra)
summary_table: P1: small prefix wins for template-heavy; P4 best-case. P2/P3 need KV sizing, infra cost can invert ROI. Measurement/instrumentation are gating factors.
